title: Full data export as a human-readable, printable PDF packet
description: Wardens trust a physical, readable paper trail more than a zip file they can't open themselves (LODGY-28 exports a DB+photos zip, not something a warden can read or hand to someone). To ease the fear of 'losing everything in the app', offer a printable/PDF export of the underlying records - hostels, tenants, invoices, payments - as a human-readable document, distinct from the machine-readable backup zip. Depends on LODGY-56 (shared PDF rendering foundation) - reuse the same renderer LODGY-37 builds against rather than a second pipeline; this ticket is the larger, multi-page consumer of it.
acceptanceCriteria: Warden can export a printable PDF summary of all tenants, active agreements, and payment history for a hostel (or all hostels)
PDF is legible and organized (grouped by hostel/room/tenant), not a raw data dump
Exported via SAF like other exports (LODGY-23/28), so it can be saved, printed, or shared

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Added an explicit dependency on LODGY-56 - this ticket and LODGY-37 both need PDF rendering and were at risk of building two separate, inconsistent pipelines. LODGY-56 builds the shared renderer first; this ticket and LODGY-37 consume it.
Starting - the multi-page consumer of LODGY-56: a printable packet grouped hostel -> floor -> room -> tenant with agreement and payment history, exported through SAF like the other exports.

Printable records packet built on LODGY-56's renderer, the same one LODGY-37 uses - no second pipeline. pdf/DataPacket.kt structures the document hostel -> floor -> room+bed -> tenant, which is how a warden walks the property, rather than a flat dump in whatever order the database returned: per hostel a title, address and bed summary; per floor a heading; per tenancy a 'Room 204 - Bed B - Ravi' heading with phone, status, agreed rent, move-in (and move-out only when there is one), then a Period/Due/Paid/Status table of the whole invoice history - or a plain sentence where a tenancy has no invoices and where a hostel has no tenancies at all, so an empty property is still visibly present instead of silently missing. DataPacketViewModel gathers it with a scope of This hostel (default) or All hostels, counts beds from the bed rows, takes each bed's latest agreement so a moved-out tenancy still appears rather than vanishing, orders invoices oldest period first, and runs every amount through effectiveAmountDue() so the packet agrees with the rest of the app about credits. Reached from More -> Printable records (PDF), exported via the same SAF CreateDocument path as LODGY-23/28/37 as lodgy-records-<date>.pdf. Tests: DataPacketTest asserts the grouping order, the invoice table, the no-invoices and no-tenancies cases, move-out row presence, and that a 32-tenancy property paginates across pages without losing a tenancy; DataPacketViewModelTest covers scope switching, bed counts, invoice ordering with a credit applied, and beds that were never occupied. testDebugUnitTest green.

FAIL - the export works, but it prints a factually wrong statement about a current resident. AC1 and AC3 pass: More > Printable records (PDF) offers 'This hostel' / 'All hostels' with record counts, and saves via SAF (lodgy-records-2026-09-04.pdf). AC2 is mostly good - the packet is genuinely organised rather than a dump: hostel name and address, a beds summary, then floor > room > tenant with phone, status, rent and dates, and a per-tenant invoice history table with correct credit-adjusted amounts, all legible with page footers, and it renders correctly in Hindi too. THE BUG: for a tenant who is ACTIVE and has merely given notice, the packet prints 'Moved out: 20 Sep 2026'. The same record says 'Status: ACTIVE' three lines above, so the document contradicts itself and tells anyone reading it that a current resident has already left. WHAT I DID: set a planned move-out date of 20 Sep 2026 on Ramesh Kumar (still ACTIVE, bed still OCCUPIED, exactly as LODGY-49 intends), then exported the printable records packet. WHAT I EXPECTED: either no move-out line, or one clearly labelled as a planned/notice date. WHAT HAPPENED: it is labelled 'Moved out', identically to a real completed checkout. ROOT CAUSE: pdf/DataPacket.kt:77 does tenancy.moveOutDate?.let { add(PdfBlock.KeyValue(labels.movedOut, it)) } with no check of the agreement's status. LODGY-49 now writes a planned moveOutDate onto ACTIVE agreements, so that field no longer means 'has moved out'. SUGGESTED FIX: branch on agreement status - label it 'Moved out' only for a CLOSED agreement, and use a separate 'Notice given / Leaving on' label while ACTIVE. This matters more than an ordinary display bug because the entire point of this ticket is a document the warden prints and hands to someone.

Fixed. pdf/DataPacket.kt no longer assumes a moveOutDate means a completed departure: PacketTenancy gains `moveOutIsPlanned`, PacketLabels gains `noticeGiven`, and the block picks the label by that flag. DataPacketScreen passes `moveOutIsPlanned = tenancy.active`, using the `active` flag already carried on PacketTenancyData - so an ACTIVE agreement with a notice date reads as notice, and only a CLOSED one reads as a departure. New strings packet_notice_given in values/ ('Leaving on (notice given)') and values-hi/. VERIFIED ON EMULATOR with one export that exercises BOTH branches in a single document: Ramesh Kumar (VACATED, real checkout) prints 'Moved out: 4 Sep 2026', and Suresh (ACTIVE, notice set for 25 Sep 2026) prints 'Leaving on (notice given): 25 Sep 2026'. The self-contradiction QA found - a record saying ACTIVE three lines above 'Moved out' - is gone. Added two DataPacketTest cases asserting each branch emits the right label and not the other. Build and full suite green: 412 tests pass (4 new), ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug both successful. Tests touched for the new signatures: TenantProfileViewModelTest and TenantDirectoryViewModelTest now mock the observed agreement flows, InvoiceListViewModelTest gains the ReconciliationRepository mock, and DataPacketTest gains the noticeGiven label. Note on two profile tests: they assert state after setPlannedMoveOut, which previously passed only because the ViewModel wrote the value optimistically. Rather than keep that second source of truth - the exact bug class LODGY-33 is about - the mocks now use a MutableStateFlow that re-emits on write, which is how Room actually behaves.

PASS - the self-contradiction is gone, and one export proves both branches at once. AC1 and AC3 were already passing. The fix: I set a notice date of 25 Sep 2026 on Suresh while he was still ACTIVE with his bed still OCCUPIED (exactly the LODGY-49 state that produced the bug), then exported the printable packet with Ramesh Kumar already checked out. The single PDF contains both cases and labels them differently and correctly - Ramesh reads 'Status VACATED' then 'Moved out: 4 Sep 2026', Suresh reads 'Status ACTIVE' then 'Leaving on (notice given): 25 Sep 2026'. No record now says a current resident has moved out. AC2 still holds: the packet is still grouped hostel -> floor -> room -> tenant with per-tenant invoice history and correct credit-adjusted amounts, and the new label is translated in values-hi so the Hindi export is not left with an English string.
